clue.text: Classic poet opening, putting love first

indicators.note: first says where it goes: to the front, ahead of the remaining letters of the opening

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, which looks like the letter O

indicators.note: putting love somewhere means moving that letter out of the word for opening to a new place

parts.note: a void is a gap or opening

explanation.surface: An instruction for starting a poem: open with love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' looks like the start of a poem, but it is a gap. 'putting love first' moves the love letter from inside that word to its front.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovid was a Roman poet of the classical age, author of the Metamorphoses.

clue.text: Leave a league after lower score at rugby

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for league

explanation.surface: A club quitting its league after sinking to a lower score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' sits beside 'score' as if an adjective, but it is a verb here, and 'after' puts it first.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop goal is a kick at goal from a dropped ball, worth three points in rugby union.

clue.text: Support post established in company? On the contrary

indicators.note: swap the roles: company goes in post, not post in company

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it

explanation.surface: Someone taking up a post in a firm, then an editor's aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' reverses who holds whom, letting the surface read naturally while the wordplay runs the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: in a meeting, seconding a motion means backing or supporting it.

clue.text: More than one church feature that is included in church measures

parts.note: CE (Church of England) + METERS, units of length in US spelling

explanation.surface: Something architectural sitting inside a church's measurements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Church' appears twice: once in the definition and once, as CE, in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A churchyard burial ground is a common feature of a church; the plural matches 'more than one'.

clue.text: Promotion? Gutted third team is never working for that

indicators.note: the letters are put to work in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A football club, bottom of the league, that will never earn promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about league promotion; the definition wants the sales kind, which the question mark allows.
explanation.definitionFit: The surface's promotion is a club going up a division; the setter means publicity for a product, the job of an ad.

clue.text: Millions enthralled by older article represented as the best ever

indicators.note: the letters are presented again in a new order

explanation.surface: An antique fetching millions and being billed as the finest ever sold.
explanation.walkthrough: M joins OLDER ARTICLE and the thirteen letters are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a mark unbeaten across all history, not just this season, is the best ever.

clue.text: I note obligation to go round Malta promptly

parts.note: a tie is something that binds you
M is Malta's international vehicle code

explanation.surface: Someone noting a duty to sail round Malta without delay.
explanation.walkthrough: TIE wraps round M to make TIME after I and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: turning up before the deadline, punctually, is arriving without delay.

clue.text: Answer at 5A, not here?

definitions.meaning: the surface reading is a plain cross-reference: fill in 5 Across
the setter means a word describing ADVERTISEMENT, which has four syllables, but not describing itself, since this answer has five

explanation.surface: A cross-reference asking what 5 Across is, but not this word.
explanation.walkthrough: ADVERTISEMENT has four syllables, so it is a tetrasyllable; TETRASYLLABLE itself has five, so the word is not one: 'not here'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetrasyllable is a word of four syllables, as ADVERTISEMENT is.

clue.text: Smelly and hard, giving off sulphur

explanation.surface: A lump of something that stinks because it gives off sulphur fumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Giving off' pretends to mean emitting a smell; it means losing the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Olid is a rare word meaning foul-smelling.

clue.text: Winged figure somehow hated to kill

indicators.note: the letters of HATED come out some other way

parts.note: a putto is a winged cherub in Renaissance art

explanation.surface: A hated angel being condemned to die.
explanation.walkthrough: PUTTO is the painters' word for a chubby winged boy; the enumeration splits it across PUT TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the phrase means to execute, a formal way to kill.

clue.text: Ancient artist reached around one

indicators.note: one thing placed around another encloses it, so GOT TO is placed about I

explanation.surface: An old master who has reached about one.
explanation.walkthrough: GOT TO is two words that open after the G to take I.
explanation.definitionFit: Giotto was a Florentine painter of around 1300, ancient enough by any standard.

clue.text: Money's bringing in a lot of Shakespeare in parish buildings

parts.note: tin is slang for money; plus the S
Shakespeare is the Bard; THE BARD minus its D

explanation.surface: Cash flowing in from a Shakespeare staging put on in church halls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tin' is old British slang for money. A tithe barn stored the tenth of produce owed to the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Tithe barns were barns built to hold a parish's tithes.

clue.text: Starve, against tucking into food from a long time ago

parts.note: to starve is to die of hunger

explanation.surface: A starving person who nevertheless won't tuck into ancient food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucking into' plays on eating, which fights 'Starve'; here it means going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval describes the Middle Ages, a long time ago.

clue.text: Praises fruit found around Texas, after reflection

indicators.note: a mirror image turns the whole thing back to front

explanation.surface: Someone praising the fruit grown in Texas after some thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflection' looks like thinking it over; here it means mirror-reversing SLO-TX-E.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the verb, from Latin for 'raise up', means to praise highly.

clue.text: Become weary in Year Five, backsliding in fact

indicators.note: backsliding means sliding back, so the whole assembly is read in reverse
in places the word for become weary inside the year and five letters

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
to tire is to become weary

explanation.surface: A pupil grows weary in Year Five and in fact slips back in their schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Year Five' looks like a school year; it is Y and V, with TIRE between them, giving YTIREV, which 'backsliding' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Verity means truth, a true statement or fact; the phrase in verity means in fact.

clue.text: Apparatus with the same size of manual?

parts.note: the prefix meaning equal, as in equidistant

explanation.surface: Kit that comes with a handbook of the same dimensions.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the loose PAGE: a page is the unit a manual's size is counted in.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipage is an old word for equipment or apparatus.

clue.text: Heading for life in open country implies wellbeing

indicators.note: in puts that letter inside the word for open country

parts.note: a heath is open, uncultivated country

indicators.note: heading means the first part, so the first letter of life is taken

explanation.surface: Setting off for a life in the countryside promises wellbeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading for life' reads like moving to a new life; it gives L, which goes into HEATH.
explanation.definitionFit: Health is the state of being well in body and mind, the same as wellbeing.

clue.text: Romantic song in series English and European backed

parts.note: a Dane is one kind of European

explanation.surface: A love song in a TV series, with English and European backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European' stands for one nationality, DANE; E and DANE together turn round to give ENADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenade is a love song sung under a window.

clue.text: Film franchise: a version with a scoundrel turning up

parts.note: V is an abbreviation for version, as in Bible translations

indicators.note: turning up means flipped upward, so in this down entry the word for scoundrel is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a rat is a scoundrel or traitor

explanation.surface: A film series gets a new version featuring a villain who appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' sounds like a villain arriving, but it reverses the scoundrel upward in the down grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Avatar is James Cameron's blockbuster science-fiction film series set on the moon Pandora.

clue.text: You are texting us about the French Bond girl?

parts.note: in text messages you are is shortened to the two letters that sound like it

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so us is read backwards

parts.note: la is the French for the, feminine

explanation.surface: Someone asks, by text message, whether we are the Bond girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'texting' tells you to use text-speak: U for you and R for are.
explanation.definitionFit: Ursula Andress played Honey Ryder in Dr No, making her the first famous Bond girl.

clue.text: Something-or-other circles traffic hold-up with a quick flight

explanation.surface: A gadget that dodges traffic jams by hopping into the air.
explanation.walkthrough: OOJAMAFLIP is British slang for a thing whose name escapes you, like thingamajig.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang: a jokey placeholder for any object whose name you have forgotten.

clue.text: Obligation due but university always slipping away

indicators.note: university is U, and always slipping away means every U goes, both of them from due but

explanation.surface: A student has a payment due, but the university is forever losing track of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove both Us from DUE BUT and DEBT is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt is money owed, an obligation to pay.

clue.text: Members of synod, i.e. the governing body

indicators.note: the answer is made of parts of the following words

explanation.surface: Members of a church synod described as its ruling body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Members of' looks like people on the synod; it means letters from the words.
explanation.definitionFit: A diet is a legislative assembly, as in the Japanese Diet.

clue.text: Medical approach that's treated gland in the eye? Yes and no

indicators.note: treated means processed or dealt with, so the letters of gland in the eye are reworked

explanation.surface: A doctor asks whether a method involved treating a gland in the eye, and gets an equivocal answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yes and no' comments on the surface: it is treatment, but for teeth, not eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Dental hygiene is the practice of keeping teeth and gums clean to prevent disease, a preventive medical approach.
